All 48 distinct files in SOURCES.tsv matched their SHA-256 and size (30,757,139 bytes in total). I read the legend, axes and filled WT cagrilintide bars in Figure 6a–c from gr6.jpg, also fetched independently from PMC Open Access. Relative to WT vehicle in MBH they give 404 total, 96 up and 308 down. Study 3 initially assigned eight male mice per treatment group and specified 3 nmol/kg daily for 21 days, consistent with the series summary. The eight treated WT ARC GSMs say 0.3 nmol/kg. The tissue was a bilateral MBH punch including ARC/VMN. The caption reports six mice per group. The paper gives 117 of 138 brain samples passing pre-sequencing QC and two later ARC CountQC exclusions with no group or GSM assignment.

SOFT, the live GEO TAR and the ENA run report agree on 116 samples, 116 individual abundance files and 116 unique runs with matching GSM aliases. The series matrix has a header and zero feature rows. The ENA analysis report contains only its header. The registered samplesheet, SOFT and provenance agree on vehicle GSM8971569–GSM8971575 (Brain_region_93–99) and treated GSM8971462–GSM8971469 (Brain_region_100–107). Each of the 15 compressed files, including its TAR copy, matches its registered source hash. The family SOFT also matches its pin. Each library has the same 121,798 distinct ENSMUST transcript IDs and five kallisto fields (target_id, length, eff_length, est_counts, tpm). If six in each final WT group came from these 15 deposits, one vehicle and two treated libraries would be outside the figure. Their identities remain unknown.

For the registered arcuate track and cagrilintide_vs_vehicle contrast, I verified case minus control against the group means of the pinned log2(gene-summed TPM + 1) expression matrix. All 28,705 published logFC values agreed to within 5.2 × 10^-15. Applying the registered variance filter to the published matrix recovered the same 28,705 unique symbols. Using the pinned GRCm39 release 113 transcript-to-gene annotation, the deposited TPMs and the registered feature map, I independently recovered 10 tested unmapped rows out of 22, for 28,715 tested rows in the BH family. Recounting the published limma DE table gave 0 at BH adjusted P < 0.05, 2,985 at raw P < 0.05 (2,146 up, 839 down), and minimum published adjusted P 0.0643336618892822. The DE and samplesheet hashes match provenance. The old manual ledger's 2,997 nominal calls and approximate minimum of 0.0646355 do not describe this output.

The final paper identifies the SUSHI DESeq2App. Its general P < 0.05 statement and separate WGCNA criteria do not specify how Figure 6 DEGs were called. Figure 7 addresses genotype and modules. I found 0 pairable author gene-level treatment effects in the material examined. The figure supplies neither gene identities nor the author tested universe. Reference coverage, correlations, same-gene sign agreement and paired P/FDR remain unassessed under author-concordance-v2. The two 0.05 counts summarize the full registered table. No subgroup or cutoff was fitted to 404.

Only manual-review.json and verification-review.json contain a record for this dataset among the five ledgers. I verified each proposed enum, evidence-link kind and empty sign-off list against existing ledger entries. The corrected proposal passes check_proposals.cjs. The figure is accessible aggregate evidence, so partial availability, unresolved outcome and needs_author_contact are justified. The archive, method and figure leave the exact WT cohort and per-gene results open. The independent replay is refute/recheck.py --gtf.
problems: The proposal omits a discrepancy in the authors' own account. The published Results and GEO series summary limit the absence of WT DEGs to DVC and LPBN, but the final Discussion makes a broader statement about the absence of a treatment effect. The indexed February 2025 SSRN abstract extends that claim across regions and genotypes. The corrected proposal records the version and section for each claim and asks which analysis the Discussion describes. Figure 6 remains the quantitative reference for WT MBH.

Several phrases present six mice per arm as the final analyzed cohort. Six is the caption's reported number. Study 3 assigned eight per arm, and neither the paper nor the deposit identifies the final libraries. The corrected proposal keeps the one-vehicle/two-treated difference conditional on the caption and on membership in the deposit.

The Europe PMC supplementary endpoint returned a 292-byte XML connection-error response on a repeat request, despite HTTP 200. Its previously retained ZIP is valid. The corrected proposal links directly to the verified PMC Open Access Figure 6 image and retains the publisher appendix link.
